  Pursuant to State and County Directives, the physical access to the meeting has been suspended.

  discriminatory language, will not be read.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 19, 2021
   C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – SEPTEMBER 2021

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2021-22 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 21-30 dated July 20, 2021) and California Government
  Code §53646, the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the
  City Council, City Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The
  September 2021 Cash and Investment Report is presented to receive and file
  in accordance with the City’s adopted 2021-22 Investment Policy.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for September 2021.

  D. BUDGET UPDATE – FISCAL YEAR 2020-21 AND FISCAL YEAR 2021-22

  This report provides a budget update as of September 30, 2021, for the City’s
  General Fund and Mission Playhouse for fiscal years 2020-21 and 2021-22.
  This update is provided during the period when the City is closing the fiscal
  year that ended on June 30th and beginning the fiscal year that started on July
  1st. The fiscal year 2020-21 final projected numbers are unaudited.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the report.

  E. FISCAL YEAR 2020-21 YEAR-END APPROPRIATION ADJUSTMENTS

  Budget transfers from one department to another that are greater than
  $15,000 require City Council approval. Additionally, General Fund
  departments that exceed the department budget are disclosed in the audited
  financial statements. Finally, City funds should not exceed the approved
  appropriations. This report proposes transfers within funds that are greater
  than $15,000 and proposes to increase appropriations where expenditures
  exceeded the approved budget to prepare the financial statements for the
  upcoming audit.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 21-48,
  approving proposed amendments to the Annual Budget for Fiscal Year 2020-
  21.

  3
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 19, 2021
   F. ORDINANCE NO. 680, AMENDING TITLE V: “PUBLIC WORKS” OF THE
  SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE BY ADDING CHAPTER 50.016,
  “MANDATORY ORGANIC WASTE DISPOSAL REGULATIONS” AND
  ORDINANCE NO. 681, AMENDING TITLE III: “ADMINISTRATION”
  CHAPTER 34: “FINANCE AND REVENUE” OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  MUNICIPAL CODE BY ADDING SECTION 34.80 “RECOVERED ORGANIC
  WASTE PRODUCT PROCUREMENT POLICY” INTRODUCTION

  Senate Bill 1383 (“SB 1383), the Short-lived Climate Pollutant Reduction Act
  of 2016, requires the California Department of Resources, Recycling, and
  Recovery (“CalRecycle”) to develop regulations to reduce organics in landfills
  as a source of methane. The regulations place requirements on multiple
  entities including cities, residential households, commercial businesses,
  business owners, edible food generators, food recover organizations, food
  recovery services and waste haulers to support achievement of statewide
  organic waste disposal reduction targets. SB 1383 requires cities to adopt and
  enforce an ordinance or enforceable mechanism to implement relevant
  provisions of SB 1383 Regulations.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Introduce and conduct the first reading by title only of: “Ordinance No.
  680, Amending Title V: “Public Works” of the San Gabriel Municipal Code
  by adding Chapter 50.016, “Mandatory Organic Waste Disposal
  Regulations”; and Ordinance No. 681, Amending Title III: “Administration”
  Chapter 34: “Finance and Revenue” of the San Gabriel Municipal Code by
  adding Section 34.80 “Recovered Organic Waste Product Procurement
  Policy.”
  2. Schedule second reading and adoption of both Ordinances for the next
  regular City Council meeting on November 2, 2021.

  G. ADOPTION AND SECOND READING OF ORDINANCE NO. 679:
  AMENDING CHAPTER 153 (ZONING) OF THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL
  CODE RELATING TO TERM LIMITS FOR THE HISTORIC PRESERVATION
  AND CULTURAL RESOURCE COMMISSION (PLANNING CASE NO. ZTA21-
  001)

  Adoption of Ordinance No. 679 would amend the code relating to term limits
  for the Historic Preservation and Cultural Resource Commission and
  Nomination Procedures for Historic Resources.

  4
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 19, 2021
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council conduct second reading by title only
  and adopt Ordinance No. 679 entitled, “An Ordinance of the City Council of
  the City of San Gabriel, California, Approving Planning Case No. ZTA21-001,
  Amending Title XV, Chapter 153 (Zoning) Relating to Term Limits and
  Nomination Procedures for Historic Resources”.

  H. ADOPTION AT SECOND READING OF ORDINANCE NO. 678: ZONE
  CHANGE/PLANNED DEVELOPMENT OVERLAY AND A DEVELOPMENT
  AGREEMENT FOR THE PACIFIC SQUARE MIXED-USE PROJECT
  (PLANNING CASE NO. ZC18-001; 700-800 SOUTH SAN GABRIEL
  BOULEVARD)

  Adoption of Ordinance No. 678 would change the Zoning of properties at
  700-800 South San Gabriel Boulevard from C-1 to C-1/PD and approve the
  Development Agreement. The introduction and first reading of Ordinance No.
  678 was conducted with a 4-1 vote of the City Council at the September 21,
  2021 Regular City Council Meeting.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive second reading and adopt
  Ordinance No. 678 entitled, “An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of
  San Gabriel, California, Approving Planning Case No. ZC18-001, for a Zone
  Change/Planned Development Overlay and a Development Agreement for
  the Pacific Square Mixed-Use Project Located at 700-800 South San Gabriel
  Boulevard.”

  I. FIREWORK DISPLAY PERMIT – GABRIELINO HIGH SCHOOL

  Fireworks & Stage FX America, Incorporated (Fireworks America), a California
  State Licensed Pyrotechnics Company, has applied for a permit on behalf of
  Gabrielino High School to conduct a two-minute, low level pyrotechnic
  display for an event on the school athletic field on October 21, 2021.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the Deputy Fire Marshal to
  issue a Fireworks Permit to Fireworks America contingent on the meeting the
  conditions to the application.

  5
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 19, 2021
   J. SELECTIVE TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT PROGRAM (STEP) GRANT

  The Police Department has received a renewed grant from the Office of Traffic
  Safety (OTS) to participate in the Selective Traffic Enforcement Program (STEP)
  for Federal Fiscal Year 2021-2022. The grant will reimburse the City for
  personnel overtime costs incurred to participate in this campaign and for the
  purchase of related equipment and training in the sum of $76,000. In addition,
  this report is intended to approve the resolution to amend the current budget
  to approve the allocation of funds not to exceed the amount of $76,000 to be
  reimbursed by OTS based on actual funds used during the Federal Fiscal Year
  Grant (10-01-2021 through 09-30-2022).

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 21-46
  approving and accepting the OTS contract funding outlined in this staff report
  and increase the Revenue Budget Account 147-3229 by an estimated $76,000,
  account 147-751-00, which will be used for overtime costs and the purchase
  of any related equipment.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. COMPREHENSIVE FINANCIAL RECOVERY PLAN AND ANALYSIS OF THE
  STATE AUDITOR FINANCIAL RANKINGS

  In February 2020, the California State Auditor was directed by the Joint
  Legislative Audit Committee to conduct an audit of the City of San Gabriel.
  On April 27, 2021, the California State Auditor provided the City their
  completed audit report. The audit report detailed twelve recommendations,
  one being the adoption by the City Council of a comprehensive financial
  recovery plan. This report presents the comprehensive recovery plan along
  with an analysis on city financial rankings that are published by the State
  Auditor.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the comprehensive financial
  recovery plan as required by the State Auditor.

  6
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 19, 2021
   B. PRESENTATION ON EXPANDED TRANSIT SERVICES

  The City of San Gabriel contracts with a transit provider, First Transit, to
  manage and operate a Dial-A-Ride service for City residents age 62 and over
  and individuals with disabilities. The City Council has expressed interest in
  reviewing an expanded service model that would reach more residents and at
  their first meeting on February 16, 2021, approved an extension of the
  contract with First Transit to allow staff time to review and provide transit
  options for Council’s consideration.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive the presentation from First
  Transit on expanded transit services and direct staff to proceed with one of
  three options:
  1. Return with a contract proposal to initiate a microtransit program with
  First Transit for 3 years.
  2. Complete a Request for Proposal for a similar model.
  3. Continue with the Dial-A-Ride service and not microtransit and enter into
  a new three-year contract with First Transit, based on the current proposal
  for the existing service model.

  C. STATE ADOPTED HOUSING LEGISLATION (SENATE BILL 8, SENATE BILL
  9, AND SENATE BILL 10)

  Over the recent years, the State of California has been in an ongoing housing
  supply crisis. This has led to a number of bills being signed and adopted at
  the State level to help alleviate the housing shortage. On September 16, 2021,
  Governor Gavin Newsom signed multiple housing bills (SB 8, SB 9, and SB 10)
  into effect in an effort to address this housing shortage problem. The report
  provides a summary of the three recently signed bills as a basis for City
  Council discussion.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review and discuss the three
  legislative bills, provide direction to staff on the development of objective
  standards, and then direct staff to draft an Ordinance for review and
  recommendation by the Planning Commission before returning to the City
  Council for formal adoption.
